title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
authors: Florian Matz, Paul G. Graf, Markus Penz, Christian Schilling
abstract: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory to include a temperature dimension. This gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. The framework formally unifies information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation (TAO-)DFT as special cases, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set derived from biphenyl. The results help to clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.
summary: This paper introduces thermally enhanced hybrid functionals by extending the adiabatic connection principle of DFT to include a temperature dimension. This framework allows for the simultaneous, systematic treatment of both static and dynamic electron correlation effects. It establishes a powerful, general methodology for improving the accuracy and efficiency of electronic structure calculations for strongly correlated systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a computationally manageable method to simultaneously capture both static and dynamic electron correlation effects in electronic structure theory.
main_result: The authors propose 'thermally enhanced hybrid functionals' that systematically treat both correlation types by extending the adiabatic connection concept to include a temperature dimension.
method: The method extends DFT by incorporating a temperature parameter ($	au$) into the adiabatic connection, leading to functionals derived from the grand potential ($\Omega_{\lambda,	au}$) in the Gibbs ensemble.
model_or_system: The theory applies to the electronic structure of many-body systems (molecules), described by a Hamiltonian parameterized by interaction strength ($\lambda$) and temperature ($	au$).
key_observables: Free energy ($F_{\lambda,	au}$), one-particle density ($ho$), kinetic energy ($T_{\lambda,	au}$), and interaction energy ($W_{\lambda,	au}$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($\lambda$), effective temperature ($	au$), and mixing parameters ($a$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the assumption of v-representability, and the authors discuss the theoretical difficulty regarding the uniqueness of the potential at zero temperature.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the thermodynamic structure of DFT by extending the adiabatic connection to include temperature. It then derives the functional form for the exchange-correlation energy ($E_{	heta}^{xc}$) using a two-step approximation, unifying existing theories like i-DMFT and TAO-DFT.
why_interesting: This work provides a systematic, low-cost theoretical route to treat complex correlation effects (static and dynamic) that are crucial in understanding strongly correlated materials, bridging concepts from finite-temperature statistical mechanics into electronic structure theory.
